title: Sum a list
description:
Read a list of integers and print their sum.

**Input.** The first line holds `n` (1 <= n <= 1000). The second line holds `n` integers, each between -10^9 and 10^9.

**Output.** One line with the sum.

Submit a Python 3 program that reads from standard input and writes to standard output. It runs once per test, and every test must pass.

hints.body: `sys.stdin.read().split()` gives every number in the input as a list of strings, whatever the line breaks.

title: Range sums
description:
You get an array and many questions of the form "what is the sum of elements `l` through `r`?". Answer them all.

**Input.** The first line holds `n` and `q` (1 <= n <= 200000, 1 <= q <= 50000). The second line holds `a_1 ... a_n`, each between -10^9 and 10^9. Then `q` lines follow, each with `l r` (1 <= l <= r <= n).

**Output.** `q` lines, the sum `a_l + ... + a_r` for each question in order.

The time limit is 2 seconds per test, and the largest tests are at the maximum size.

title: Pair count
description:
Count the pairs of positions `i < j` with `a_i + a_j = k`.

**Input.** The first line holds `n` and `k` (1 <= n <= 200000, -2*10^9 <= k <= 2*10^9). The second line holds `a_1 ... a_n`, each between -10^9 and 10^9.

**Output.** One line with the number of pairs. It can be larger than 2^32.

The time limit is 2 seconds per test, and the largest tests are at the maximum size.
